newsitem.title: EGYPT: EGYPTIAN PARLIAMENT EXTENDS EMERGENCY LAW.
newsitem.headline: EGYPTIAN PARLIAMENT EXTENDS EMERGENCY LAW.

text.p: Egypt's parliament has approved a presidential decree to extend for three more years the emergency law in force since President Anwar Sadat was assassinated in 1981.

In a session late on Sunday, the 444-seat house passed the law after 432 members voted for its extension while only 12 voted against it. The ruling National Democratic Party has a 317-seat majority in parliament.

On Sunday, Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri described the extension as protection for Egypt's expanding economy from sabotage by "terrorists", the government's term for Moslem militants fighting to turn Egypt into a purist Islamic state.

Moslem militants have often targeted tourists, Christians and government officials in their campaign to topple the government. More than 1,000 people have died in the five years of political violence.

Emergency law has been in place in Egypt since Moslem militant gunmen killed Sadat at a military parade in 1981. Parliament has extended it regularly ever since, despite protests by leftist and liberal opposition groups.
Emergency law enables the authorities to hold detainees without charges for long periods and to try civilians in military courts, where defendants have fewer rights.
